correctness.rationale: Use u=(1-cos theta)/2 and normalized spin Wigner densities 3(1-u)^2, 6u(1-u),3u², each integrating to 1. Integrate over u in [0,p]∪[1-q,1]; orthogonal azimuthal orders diagonalize the restriction. For p>=q write d=p-q in [0,h]. Lambda_-1-lambda_+1=3d(1-h)>=0; lambda_0=h²(3-h)/2+3(1-h)d²/2 is strictly increasing for d>0, while lambda_+1 strictly decreases on [0,h]. Their difference equals (3/4)(1-h)(3d²+2d+h²-2h), negative at d0, positive at dh and with one root d*. This gives exact unique (up to reflection) global maximin, multiplicity two and strict improvement. Taylor d*=h-2h²+O(h³) yields q*=h²+O(h³) and 2:1 asymptotics. Independently evaluated h=.1,.5,.9 polynomial eigenvalues and equality at d*, and inspected symbolic/numerical checker; finite tests not needed for global proof.

final_claim: For the pure degree-one spin-weight +1 spherical-harmonic three-dimensional space and two opposite polar caps with total full-sphere area fraction h in (0,1), the only maximin least-energy allocations are the mirror pair p=(h+d*)/2,q=(h-d*)/2 with d*=(sqrt(1+6h-3h²)-1)/3. The least concentration eigenvalue has multiplicity 2; equal caps are strictly worse and their small-h maximin energy is asymptotically half the optimum.
